paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose the student union of your university is organizing an online discussion on college students doing community service. You are to write an essay on its benefits and the service you can provide to the community. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您所在大学的学生会正在组织一场关于大学生社区服务的在线讨论。您要写一篇关于其好处以及您可以为社区提供的服务的文章。您将有 30 分钟的时间来完成该任务。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Whether you’re just having a down day or a down period, taking a walk can instantly lift your mood, especially when you go outdoors. Not only can walking make you less depressed, but according to a new study, depression sufferers who took a 26 walk showed just as much improvement in their 27 as people taking medicine. In fact, 60-70 percent of the participants in the study could no longer even be 28 as depressed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无论您只是心情低落还是情绪低落，散步都可以立即提升您的心情，尤其是当您外出时。散步不仅可以减轻抑郁，而且根据一项新的研究，每天散步的抑郁症患者的症状改善程度与服药的人一样多。事实上，60-70% 的研究参与者甚至不能再被归类为抑郁症。

paragraphs.sourceText: Bone density may not be one of the most exciting health benefits of walking, but it’s an important one. People with stronger bones avoid osteoporosis (骨质疏松症) and all the problems that 29 with it, like breaks and other disabilities. And the best way to get strong, healthy bones is by doing weight-bearing exercises like running, dancing and walking, according to a large study. But as regards bones, it’s 30 use it or lose it: To keep your bones strong you have to keep exercising. The researchers found that adults who walked regularly had better bone density throughout their lives than their 31 friends.
paragraphs.translationZh: 骨密度可能不是步行最令人兴奋的健康益处之一，但它是一项重要的益处。骨骼更强壮的人可以避免骨质疏松症以及随之而来的所有问题，例如骨折和其他残疾。一项大型研究表明，获得强健、健康骨骼的最佳方法是进行跑步、跳舞和步行等负重运动。但对于骨骼来说，绝对是用进废退：要保持骨骼强健，就必须坚持锻炼。研究人员发现，经常散步的成年人一生中的骨密度比不运动的朋友更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: Taking a walk can be great for 32 your head or blowing off some steam. It also provides a great opportunity to 33 with friends and family, far away from electronics and other 34 at home. Even better, you set a powerful example because when they see you 35 the benefits of walking, they’ll be encouraged to walk more, too.
paragraphs.translationZh: 散步可以很好地让你头脑清醒或发泄一下。它还提供了一个与朋友和家人建立联系的绝佳机会，远离家中的电子产品和其他干扰。更好的是，你树立了一个强有力的榜样，因为当他们看到你从步行中获益时，他们也会被鼓励多走路。

paragraphs.sourceText: A Club Where Lions Dance and Traditions Take Root
paragraphs.translationZh: 舞狮和传统扎根的俱乐部

paragraphs.sourceText: A) The first thing you notice in the staircase to the fourth-floor studio on Canal Street in Manhattan, New York, is the measured thumping (嘭嘭声) coming from behind a metal door. Just beyond the entrance, large lion masks were twisting and turning to the drum-beat. On a recent Friday evening, the teenagers made their way across the studio floor as they practiced Chinese lion dancing.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 在通往纽约曼哈顿运河街四楼工作室的楼梯上，你首先注意到的是从金属门后面传来的有节奏的重击声（嘭嘭声）。就在入口处，巨大的狮子面具随着鼓点扭动。最近的一个周五晚上，青少年们一边练习中国舞狮，一边穿过工作室地板。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) “You want to play in a circle” Victor Fong, aged 24, told his students at the New York Chinese Freemasons Athletic Club. “Take it slow and do it again.” The dance group, made up of 60 members, performs throughout the year but was now preparing for its biggest events Chinese Lunar New Year celebrations, which will begin on Saturday and conclude on February 15. Teenagers comprise about half of the group, many of whom began lion dancing at the age of
paragraphs.translationZh: B) “你想围成一圈玩”，24 岁的维克多·方 (Victor Fong) 告诉他在纽约华人共济会体育俱乐部的学生。 “慢慢来，再做一次。”该舞蹈团由 60 名成员组成，全年演出，但目前正在为中国农历新年庆祝活动做准备，该庆祝活动将于周六开始，并于 2 月 15 日结束。该团体约一半是青少年，其中许多人从 1 岁就开始舞狮。

paragraphs.sourceText: 14. About 100 current and past members of the dance group — which has been performing since 1956 — will be among the 220 groups marching through Chinatown in Manhattan for the 18th Lunar New Year Parade on February 5.
paragraphs.translationZh: 14. 该舞蹈团自 1956 年以来一直在表演，约有 100 名现任和前任成员，将于 2 月 5 日与 220 个团体一起在曼哈顿唐人街游行，参加第 18 届农历新年游行。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Mr. Fong has been involved in the organization since he was 15 and began teaching lion dancing three years ago. But the club also acts as a recreation center and safe haven( 庇护所) for teenagers, with video games readily available. As many as 20 students show up after school. “The basic requirement for hanging out here is you have to learn how to lion dance,” Mr. Fong said. While that is not a formal requirement for being a member, everyone finds a way to participate in the Lunar New Year Parade, whether it’s by dancing, carrying a flag or beating a drum.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 方先生从 15 岁起就参与该组织，并于三年前开始教授舞狮。但该俱乐部也是青少年的娱乐中心和避风港，提供电子游戏。放学后有多达 20 名学生出现。 “在这里闲逛的基本要求是你必须学会​​舞狮，”方先生说。虽然这不是成为会员的正式要求，但每个人都想方设法参加农历新年游行，无论是跳舞、举旗还是敲鼓。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Alvin Chau, aged 26, is an environmental consultant by day and a lion dancer on weekends. He has been a club member for 10 years and joined because of an interest in lion dance. “We’re a big family,” he said, shaking hands with other members as they walked through the door. “You know everyone.”
paragraphs.translationZh: D) Alvin Chau，26岁，白天是环境顾问，周末是舞狮者。他已经成为俱乐部会员10年了，因为对舞狮的兴趣而加入。 “我们是一个大家庭，”他说，并在其他成员走进门时与他们握手。 “你认识所有人。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) It is believed that the lion dance began in the third century. Stories vary about how lion dancing came to be, but most of them include a monster named Nian who would terrorize a village. The villagers finally banded together and scared the beast away with firecrackers (爆竹) and drums. While lions are not native to China, some versions of the story include the villagers creating a monster of their own in the shape of a lion to fight off the beast.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 据信舞狮始于三世纪。关于舞狮的起源有不同的故事，但大多数故事都提到了一个名叫“年”的怪物，它会恐吓一个村庄。村民们终于联合起来，用爆竹和鼓把野兽吓跑了。虽然狮子不是中国的本土物种，但故事的某些版本包括村民创造了自己的狮子形状的怪物来对抗野兽。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Today, the dancers travel across Chinatown going from business to business to bring good luck for the coming year. The new year — according to the Chinese lunar calendar — will begin on Saturday and marks the Year of the Rooster (鸡年), which is thought to be a symbol of positivity. “It’s almost like the dark night is ending and the sun is coming up,” said Ya Yung Teng, the digital collections coordinator for the Museum of Chinese in America. “It’s hopeful that we’re going to have a new day.” Roosters and chickens are not particularly strong creatures, Ms. Teng said, but they are numerous. “In a way,” she said, the rooster “stands for ‘We the People.’ ”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 今天，舞者们穿越唐人街，从一家企业到另一家企业，为来年带来好运。根据中国农历，新的一年将于周六开始，标志着鸡年，鸡年被认为是积极的象征。 “这几乎就像黑夜正在结束，太阳正在升起，”美国华人博物馆的数字馆藏协调员亚勇腾说。 “希望我们能迎来新的一天。”滕女士说，公鸡和小鸡并不是特别强壮的动物，但数量很多。 “在某种程度上，”她说，公鸡“代表‘我们人民’。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) The lion head and tail are operated by two people. As one person controls the head, a second follows under a train of fabric representing the body. The dancers move in harmony as they imitate the animal’s natural movements in the wild, including the aggressiveness of an attack. A lion head figure weighs under 10 pounds and sits squarely on the dancer’s shoulders. Inside, the dancer manipulates strings that open and close the lion’s eyes, shake its ears and open its mouth to reveal a fire-orange tongue.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 狮头、狮尾由两人操作。当一个人控制头部时，另一个人跟随在一排代表身体的织物下面。舞者们模仿动物在野外的自然动作，包括攻击时的攻击性，动作协调一致。狮头雕像重量不到 10 磅，端正地坐在舞者的肩膀上。在里面，舞者操纵绳子打开和关闭狮子的眼睛，摇动耳朵并张开嘴巴露出火橙色的舌头。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) “A good lion dancer will imitate a living creature,” said Karlin Chan, aged 59, who heads the athletic club’s community public relations. “I started lion dancing when I was a kid,” he said. “Chinatown was much smaller then and it was a celebration with fireworks and firecrackers, which added a lot of flavor and meaning to it.”
paragraphs.translationZh: H) “优秀的舞狮者会模仿生物，”59 岁的运动俱乐部社区公共关系负责人卡林·陈 (Karlin Chan) 说。 “我小时候就开始舞狮，”他说。 “当时的唐人街要小得多，庆祝活动有烟花爆竹，这给它增添了很多味道和意义。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Mr. Chan buys a new lion head each year when he travels to China. A head costs about $1,500. “If you want the good stuff, the quality, you have to see it for yourself,” he said. “I’ll inspect the product before we put it in the container and ship it over.” Mr. Chan, who has been involved with the club for nearly 50 years, said that passing the dance from one generation to the next was vital. “You need to pass on the traditions and the culture, and this is a part of our culture,” he said. “It’s a great way to promote cultural understanding and exchange; we welcome that.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 陈先生每年去中国旅行时都会购买一个新的狮子头。一个头的价格约为 1,500 美元。 “如果你想要好东西、高品质，你就必须亲自去看看，”他说。 “在将产品放入集装箱并运送过来之前，我会检查产品。”与俱乐部打交道近50年的陈先生表示，将舞蹈代代相传至关重要。 “你需要传承传统和文化，这是我们文化的一部分，”他说。 “这是促进文化理解和交流的好方法；我们对此表示欢迎。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) For Sara Pore, aged 17, another club member, lion dance is more than just tradition; it provides a creative outlet. “Lion dancing started 2,000 years ago — that’s incredible,” she said. “But what makes you a competent lion dancer is that there’s a sense of imagination involved. Lion dancing teaches competence in leadership because of this. You’re constantly forced to push yourself past your limit.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 对于另一位俱乐部成员、17 岁的萨拉·波雷 (Sara Pore) 来说，舞狮不仅仅是传统；它提供了一个创造性的出口。 “舞狮运动始于 2000 年前——这太不可思议了，”她说。 “但是，让你成为一名称职的舞狮者的关键在于想象力。因此，舞狮可以培养领导能力。你不断被迫超越自己的极限。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Back at rehearsal (排练), Justin Le, aged 18, tied a red ribbon around his waist to practice jumping. The dancers use the ribbons to pull themselves up over their partners’ heads. The room’s ceilings are too low to wear the lion heads for jumping practice, so once up on his partner’s head, Mr. Le held out his arms as if in offering.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 回到排练时，18岁的Justin Le在腰间系了一条红丝带练习跳跃。舞者用丝带将自己拉到舞伴的头上。房间的天花板太低，无法佩戴狮头进行跳跃练习，所以当乐先生爬到搭档的头上时，他就伸出双臂，仿佛在献上。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Mr. Le comes by the dance as a legacy (传承). “I was born into it,” Mr. Le said, noting that his uncle and father were club members. “Growing up, I would always watch my family and see the lion dance, and I slowly grew interested in it.” By the age of 14, he was fully enrolled in the athletic club’s lion dance group. “I value my culture and tradition, being Chinese or Asian-American. I have a lot of pride in that,” he said. “I want to contribute and give back to the community.”
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 乐先生通过舞蹈作为遗产（传承）而来。 “我生来就是这样的，”乐先生说，并指出他的叔叔和父亲都是俱乐部成员。 “从小到大，我总是看着家人，看舞狮，慢慢地就对它产生了兴趣。” 14岁时，他正式加入了体育俱乐部的舞狮队。 “作为中国人或亚裔美国人，我重视我的文化和传统。我对此感到非常自豪，”他说。 “我想为社会做出贡献并回馈社会。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. The lion dancers perform from door to door to bring New Year wishes to business people.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36、舞狮者挨家挨户表演，为商界人士送去新年祝福。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The New York dance club also serves as a place for entertainment where youngsters can enjoy themselves safely.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 纽约舞蹈俱乐部也是青少年可以安全娱乐的娱乐场所。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Lion dancers need to have a little imagination to perform well.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38、舞狮者需要有一点想象力才能表演得好。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. There are a number of different versions about the origin of the lion dance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 关于舞狮的起源有许多不同的版本。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Some 50% of the members of a New York lion dance club are teenagers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 纽约舞狮俱乐部大约 50% 的成员是青少年。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. One club member says he feels proud of his cultural tradition.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 一位俱乐部成员说，他为自己的文化传统感到自豪。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Two dancers coordinate their movements, one manipulating the lion’s head and the other its body.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 两名舞者协调动作，一名舞者操纵狮子的头部，另一名舞者操纵狮子的身体。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. One lion dancer compares their New York dance club to a family.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 一位舞狮者将他们的纽约舞蹈俱乐部比作一个家庭。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Lion dance should be handed down to future generations as part of Chinese culture.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 舞狮应该作为中华文化的一部分传承给子孙后代。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. One lion dancer learned how to perform from his elders.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 一位舞狮者向他的长辈学习了如何表演。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Team-building exercises have become popular for managers trying to increase organisational and team harmony and productivity. Unfortunately many employees resent compulsory bonding and often regard these exercises as a nuisance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于试图提高组织和团队和谐度和生产力的管理者来说，团队建设练习已经变得很流行。不幸的是，许多员工讨厌强制建立联系，并常常认为这些练习很麻烦。

paragraphs.sourceText: A paper published this week by University of Sydney researchers in Social Networks has reported participants’ feelings about team-building interventions ( 干预), revealing ethical implications in forcing employees to take part.
paragraphs.translationZh: 悉尼大学研究人员本周在社交网络上发表的一篇论文报告了参与者对团队建设干预措施的感受，揭示了强迫员工参与的道德影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Many people see team building activities as a waste of time, so we decided to look in more depth at what’s behind this,” said the paper’s lead researcher, Dr Peter Matous.
paragraphs.translationZh: “许多人认为团队建设活动是浪费时间，因此我们决定更深入地研究其背后的原因，”该论文的首席研究员彼得·马图斯博士说。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Teams are formed, combined and restructured. Staff are relocated and office spaces redesigned. All this is done with the aim of improving workplace efficiency, collaboration and cohesion. But does any of this work?” said Dr Matous.
paragraphs.translationZh: “团队组建、合并和重组。员工重新安置，办公空间重新设计。所有这些都是为了提高工作效率、协作和凝聚力。但这一切有用吗？”马图斯博士说。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study found that team-building exercises which focused on the sharing of and intervening into personal attitudes and relationships between team members were considered too heavy-handed and intrusive, although the researchers say some degree of openness and vulnerability is often necessary to make deep, effective connections with colleagues.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究发现，专注于分享和干预团队成员之间个人态度和关系的团队建设活动被认为过于严厉和侵入性，尽管研究人员表示，为了与同事建立深入、有效的联系，一定程度的开放和脆弱往往是必要的。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Some participants were against team-building exercises because they were implicitly compulsory. They didn’t welcome management’s interest in their lives beyond their direct work performance,” said Matous. “Many people don’t want to be forced into having fun or making friends, especially not on top of their busy jobs. They feel management is being too nosy or trying to control their lives too much.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “一些参与者反对团队建设活动，因为它们是隐含的强制性。除了直接的工作表现之外，他们不欢迎管理层对他们的生活感兴趣，”马图斯说。 “许多人不想被迫去玩乐或结交朋友，尤其是在忙碌的工作之外。他们觉得管理层太爱管闲事，或者太试图控制他们的生活。”

paragraphs.sourceText: In this study the researchers recommended a self-disclosure (表露) approach where participants were guided through a series of questions that allowed them to increasingly disclose personal information and values. The method is well-tested and has been shown to increase interpersonal closeness. However, to be successful it must be voluntary.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在这项研究中，研究人员推荐了一种自我披露（表露）方法，引导参与者回答一系列问题，使他们能够越来越多地披露个人信息和价值观。该方法经过充分测试，已被证明可以增加人际亲密程度。然而，要想成功，就必须是自愿的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers said there are numerous schools of thought that propose differing psychological methods for strengthening relationships. “With caution, many relational methods to improve teams and organisations can be borrowed from other fields. The question is how to apply them effectively to strengthen an entire collective, which is more than just the sum of individual relationships,” said Dr Matous.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员表示，有许多学派提出了不同的心理学方法来加强人际关系。 “谨慎地说，许多改善团队和组织的关系方法可以从其他领域借鉴。问题是如何有效地应用它们来加强整个集体，而不仅仅是个人关系的总和，”马图斯博士说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are close to 58,000 homeless people in Los Angeles county. That’s a shocking and tragic number for a region that’s home to some of the richest people in the world. At last, the problem became so acute — and so visible — that Los Angeles took extraordinary action. The citizens of this county voted in November 2016 and again in March 2017 to raise their own taxes. The purpose of such action is to fund an enormous multibillion-dollar 10-year program of housing and social services for the homeless.
paragraphs.translationZh: 洛杉矶县有近 58,000 名无家可归者。对于这个世界上一些最富有的人的家乡来说，这是一个令人震惊和悲惨的数字。最后，这个问题变得如此尖锐和明显，以至于洛杉矶采取了非同寻常的行动。该县的公民于 2016 年 11 月和 2017 年 3 月再次投票决定提高自己的税收。此类行动的目的是为一项耗资数十亿美元、为期十年的无家可归者住房和社会服务计划提供资金。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a result, Los Angeles now has its best chance in decades to combat homelessness. This is an opportunity that surely all can agree must not be wasted. It is neither desirable nor morally acceptable nor practical for this county to tolerate the signs of deprivation more commonly associated with the slums (贫民窟) of Rio de Janiero.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，洛杉矶现在拥有几十年来解决无家可归问题的最佳机会。这是一个所有人都同意的机会，绝不能浪费。对于这个县来说，容忍与里约热内卢贫民窟有关的贫困迹象既不理想，在道德上也不可接受，也不实际。

paragraphs.sourceText: How did we get here? For as long as there are homeless people, there is a tendency to blame the victims themselves for their condition — to see their failure to thrive as an issue of character, of moral weakness, of laziness. But contrary to popular belief, the homeless in Los Angeles are not mostly mentally ill or drug addicted or frightening, although a sizable minority meet some of those descriptions. Today, a greater and greater proportion of people living on the streets are there because of bad luck or a series of mistakes, or because the economy forgot them — they lost a job or were evicted (逐出) or fled an abusive marriage just as the housing market was growing increasingly unforgiving.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们是怎么到这里的？只要还有无家可归的人，人们就会倾向于将自己的处境归咎于受害者——将他们未能成长视为性格、道德弱点和懒惰的问题。但与普遍看法相反的是，洛杉矶的无家可归者并不大多患有精神疾病、吸毒成瘾或令人恐惧，尽管相当一部分人符合其中一些描述。如今，越来越多的人流落街头，因为运气不好或一系列错误，或者因为经济忘记了他们——他们失业、被逐出或逃离虐待婚姻，而房地产市场却变得越来越无情。

paragraphs.sourceText: The challenges are enormous, even if everyone is pulling in the same direction. That reality was driven home this month by a new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report showing that the county’s homeless population is growing faster than the supply of new housing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 即使每个人都朝着同一个方向努力，挑战也是巨大的。本月洛杉矶无家可归者服务管理局的一份新报告清楚地表明了这一现实，该报告显示该县无家可归人口的增长速度超过了新住房的供应速度。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the world’s richest nation, homelessness on this scale should be shameful and shocking. But most Los Angeles residents are no longer either shocked or shamed. Increasingly, we are uncomfortable, annoyed, disgusted, scared or unaware. Compassion (同情心) is being replaced by resignation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在世界上最富有的国家，如此规模的无家可归者应该是可耻和令人震惊的。但大多数洛杉矶居民不再感到震惊或羞耻。我们越来越感到不舒服、恼怒、厌恶、害怕或不知道。同情心正在被顺从所取代。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Why did the citizens of Los Angeles vote to raise their own taxes?
paragraphs.translationZh: 51.为什么洛杉矶公民投票提高自己的税收？

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. What do people tend to believe about the homeless?
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 人们对无家可归者倾向于相信什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. What is one of the causes for more and more people in Los Angeles to become homeless?
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 洛杉矶越来越多的人无家可归的原因之一是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. What do we learn from the new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report?
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 我们从洛杉矶无家可归者服务管理局的新报告中了解到什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. How do most Los Angeles residents now feel about homelessness?
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 大多数洛杉矶居民现在对无家可归有何感想？
